name: Sort and Compare
summary: Two strings are anagrams exactly when their sorted characters match. Sort both, then compare character by character, stopping at the first difference.
visualizationIntent: init: if the lengths differ, answer is immediately false. Otherwise sort both strings and show them as two aligned character rows. loop: the i cursor compares the two rows position by position; matching positions turn green. check: the first mismatch flips answer to false and stops. return: whether the two sorted rows matched everywhere.

lineExplanations.4: Report false immediately on a length mismatch.
lineExplanations.5: Materialize the first string as a character row before sorting.
lineExplanations.6: Materialize the second string as a character row before sorting.
lineExplanations.7: Sort the first row so its characters visibly reorder.
lineExplanations.8: Sort the second row so it aligns with the first.
lineExplanations.10: Assume they match until a difference is found.
lineExplanations.12: Compare the two characters at this position.
lineExplanations.13: A mismatch means they are not anagrams.
lineExplanations.15: Otherwise advance to the next position.

syntaxExplanations.1: class Solution: defines the class wrapper expected by the platform.
syntaxExplanations.2: def isAnagram(self, s, t): receives the two strings.
syntaxExplanations.3: if len(s) != len(t): is true when the lengths differ.
syntaxExplanations.4: return False rejects strings of different lengths.
syntaxExplanations.5: s_chars = list(s) copies s into a mutable character list.
syntaxExplanations.6: t_chars = list(t) copies t into a mutable character list.
syntaxExplanations.7: s_chars.sort() reorders the first character row in place.
syntaxExplanations.8: t_chars.sort() reorders the second character row in place.
syntaxExplanations.9: i = 0 starts the comparison at the first position.
syntaxExplanations.10: answer = True assumes a match until proven otherwise.
syntaxExplanations.11: while i < len(s_chars): compares every position.
syntaxExplanations.12: if s_chars[i] != t_chars[i]: is true at the first difference.
syntaxExplanations.13: answer = False marks the strings as not anagrams.
syntaxExplanations.14: break stops at the first mismatch.
syntaxExplanations.15: i = i + 1 advances to the next position.
